# @ternent/concord

> Build a bounded application around typed commands, signed history and encrypted groups.

Published interface baseline: `npm install @ternent/concord@0.3.0-alpha.1 @ternent/armour@0.3.0-alpha.1`.
[Public README](https://github.com/ternent/core/blob/main/packages/concord/README.md).
Root declarations: `dist/index.d.ts` and its referenced model/protocol types.
Specialist exports: `/system`, `/protocol`, `/testing`.

## Define a model and author a document

```ts
import {
  defineModel,
  createDocument,
  openDocument,
  type Result,
  type ModelIssue,
} from "@ternent/concord";
import { createStandardSystemProfile } from "@ternent/concord/system";
import { generateIdentity } from "@ternent/armour";

type State = { value: string };
type Commands = { set: { value: string } };
type Event = { type: "value.set"; version: 1; data: { value: string } };
function ok<T>(value: T): Result<T, ModelIssue> {
  return { ok: true, value };
}
const invalid = (): Result<never, ModelIssue> => ({
  ok: false,
  error: { code: "VALUE_INVALID", message: "Expected a string value" },
});
function validate(input: unknown): Result<Commands["set"], ModelIssue> {
  if (
    !input ||
    typeof input !== "object" ||
    Array.isArray(input) ||
    !("value" in input) ||
    typeof input.value !== "string"
  )
    return invalid();
  return ok({ value: input.value });
}
const model = defineModel<State, Commands, Event>({
  ref: { id: "example.value", version: 1 },
  initial: () => ({ value: "" }),
  commands: {
    set: { validate, decide: (input) => ok([{ type: "value.set", version: 1, data: input }]) },
  },
  validateEvent(input) {
    if (
      !input ||
      typeof input !== "object" ||
      Array.isArray(input) ||
      !("type" in input) ||
      input.type !== "value.set" ||
      !("version" in input) ||
      input.version !== 1 ||
      !("data" in input)
    )
      return invalid();
    const data = validate(input.data);
    return data.ok ? ok({ type: "value.set", version: 1, data: data.value }) : data;
  },
  requirements: () => ["write"],
  reduce: (_state, event) => ok({ value: event.data.value }),
});
const identityResult = await generateIdentity();
if (!identityResult.ok) throw new Error(identityResult.error.code);
const identity = identityResult.value;
const system = createStandardSystemProfile();
const created = await createDocument({ model, system, identity });
if (!created.ok) throw new Error(created.error.code);
const document = created.value;
const written = await document.dispatch("set", { value: "hello" });
if (!written.ok) throw new Error(written.error.code);
const bytes = document.export();
const reopened = await openDocument({ bytes, model, system, signer: identity });
const state = reopened.state();
if (state.status !== "ready") throw new Error(reopened.inspect().findings[0]?.code);
console.log(state.projection.value);
```

The host owns the identity and chooses trusted model/system implementations. Persisting
committed document bytes does not persist the identity capability. Reopen needs those
implementations and the reader's keys to reconstruct private application state.

## Model contract

One document declares one stable model id/version. Commands validate unknown input,
then decide events against the current projection (or draft preview). validateEvent
checks recorded events during replay; reduce is pure and returns new JSON state.
requirements declares needed capabilities and is checked during authoring and replay.
Time, randomness and external reads belong in authored input, never reducers. Values
must be portable JSON with safe integers, valid Unicode and no undefined or hooks.
There is no in-place model upgrade or automatic plugin loading.

## Handle lifecycle and errors

createDocument returns Result<DocumentHandle>; openDocument returns a handle, including
read-only inspection handles for invalid, incompatible, locked or stale input.
state is either ready (projection, head, documentId, canWrite, coverage, lockedEntries)
or inspection (reason). Always narrow status before rendering a projection. inspect
exposes verification, system/application status, findings, requirements and evidence.
verify returns an integrity report; it does not certify freshness or model validity.
replay returns Result<{ projection, coverage, lockedEntries }>.
Dispatch, commit and discardDraft return structured Results. Treat thrown host or
transport failures separately. export returns Uint8Array committed bytes; inspection
exports preserve original evidence. Default dispatch immediately signs a local commit.
Publication to storage is a separate host operation.

## Drafts

Pass mode draft to create/open. dispatch stages command intents in memory; draft()
returns baseHead, entryCount and preview. state/inspect/export/verify/replay continue
to describe committed history. commit({ message: "..." }) signs the staged group;
discardDraft drops it. Empty or immediate-mode commit fails NO_DRAFT. Genesis always
commits immediately. Drafts are not exported or recovered by the library. The host
owns autosave, command retention and recovery. Commit messages are public metadata.

## Members, groups and readable replay

Import createGroup, setMember, removeMember and createStandardSystemProfile from
`@ternent/concord/system`. Genesis signer initially owns the default document group.
Capabilities are read/write/grant/administer. System changes require an immediate-mode
handle; draft mode does not implicitly switch modes. A default-group writer can
createGroup(handle), receiving an AudienceId. Additional groups have independent
memberships; document ownership does not grant their keys or administration.

setMember(handle, { audience, identity: publicIdentity, capabilities: ["read", "write"] })
admits or changes a member. Omitting audience selects document. Admission/readmission
grants that group's history. removeMember(handle, { audience, identityId }) rotates
future group encryption; historical keys/plaintext remain readable. Recipients' actual
decryptability cannot be certified by another reader. Do not implement these operations
with UI filters or by editing serialized history.

A command's audience(input) selects exactly one group (default document) before its
decision gets group-scoped facts. model.audience(event) must agree with every emitted
event and its signed envelope. A command cannot span groups; a draft can group several
commands that target different groups.

Without reduceLocked, missing private events prevent trusted application replay.
Opt into readable coverage with reduceLocked(state, { audience, epoch }, facts).
Never invent hidden event contents. A ready readable projection has incomplete
coverage; lockedEntries counts events, not distinct domain objects. Invalid reachable
signed history blocks trusted state even for groups the reader cannot decrypt.

## Storage, conflict retry and freshness

export bytes for storage. `/testing` exports ArtifactStore/ExpectedHeadArtifactStore
and copied-buffer in-memory reference stores, including createMemoryExpectedHeadStore.
They are reference implementations, not a network sync provider. Production adapters
must implement atomic expected-head writes using provider transactions or conditions.

Keep a remembered remote head and the intended commands until publication succeeds.
On an explicit HEAD_CONFLICT, retain local and remote bytes, inspect/compare snapshots,
open the accepted remote snapshot and reissue the intent under current authority.
Reissue creates new signed events and can fail validation or permission checks. Retain
local work if it fails. Do not blindly retry an uncertain transport outcome or infer
commands from encrypted event history. Runtime mutations do not publish or retry.

openDocument({ bytes, model, system, signer, anchor: rememberedSnapshotBytes }) detects
older/divergent snapshots relative to that verified anchor. Without it, valid integrity
reports freshness unanchored. Storage latest-head discovery belongs to the adapter/host.
There are no merge, fetch, push, pull or checkpoint methods in the runtime.
